summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old male with a history of chronic systolic heart failure, COPD, lung cancer after radiation therapy, atrial fibrillation, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for persistent abdominal pain lasting 1.5 months, associated with nausea, decreased oral intake, and weight loss. He also reported a syncopal episode, likely due to hypovolemia from poor intake. Initial labs showed acute kidney injury with elevated creatinine (2.4) and leukocytosis, both improving with IV fluids and holding diuretics. Abdominal pain was concerning for mesenteric ischemia given his peripheral vascular disease and smoking history, but imaging was limited. A liver biopsy was completed for an FDG-avid lesion, with results pending. His metoprolol was reduced due to orthostasis, warfarin was restarted with bridging Lovenox, and he was discharged home with instructions to monitor weight, resume diuretics if weight exceeded 207 lbs, and follow up on lab work and outpatient studies including colonoscopy and echocardiogram.
